title: Time is greater than space (Evangelii Gaudium 222)
hook: start processes rather than seize territory
tomorrow: can you love the planet and ignore the person next to you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two churches, and Francis choosing the one bruised from the street over the one shut in safe. The scuffs are the record of going out.

Some weeks you want the whole thing fixed by Friday: the friendship, the grades, the habit, the family mess. One big push, and done. Pope Francis has a principle for that urge, and its name sounds like physics: time is greater than space. It sits in Evangelii Gaudium, and he explains it with a farmer whose field comes up wheat, with weeds growing right in among it.
screen: `FIXED BY FRIDAY.` → `TIME IS GREATER THAN SPACE.` → `A FIELD OF WHEAT AND WEEDS.`

segments.voice: In Jesus's parable, the farmer's servants want to rush out and pull the weeds at once. He tells them no: you'll rip up the wheat too. Let both grow until the harvest. Francis builds on that. It's the first of four principles he gives for building a people that lives in peace. Space, in his sense, is ground you can hold right now: a position, a win, control. Time is the open horizon, where things grow. Putting time first means starting processes rather than possessing spaces. It lets you work slowly but surely, without being obsessed with quick results, and it helps you bear hard situations and plans that have to change. Then the opposite mistake: trying to hold everything together in the present, grabbing every space of power and self-assertion, freezing what ought to move. And here's the line worth repeating. Processes, he says, involve other people, who can carry them on until they bear fruit. A seized space belongs to you. A started process belongs to everyone who joins it. So patience here isn't doing nothing. The enemy's weeds are real, Francis says, but in the end the goodness of the wheat wins out. You plant something, and trust the harvest to time.
screen: `LET BOTH GROW UNTIL THE HARVEST.` · `SPACE: GROUND YOU HOLD NOW.` · `TIME: WHERE THINGS GROW.` · `OTHERS CARRY IT ON.` · then, large: `START PROCESSES.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing you've wanted to fix in a single push. Then send one short text that starts something slow instead: a standing call, a weekly walk, a first small question. If you pray, you can offer that seed to God and leave the harvest with him.
Time is greater than space. Francis's principle: start something that can grow, rather than grab ground you can hold today.
screen: `TIME IS GREATER THAN SPACE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Hold onto this: start processes, and let other people help carry them. That's the day.

screen: `DAY 1601 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: CAN YOU LOVE THE PLANET AND IGNORE YOUR NEIGHBOR?`
